AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: The present study aimed to reveal the influence of combination of different collimators and energy windows on the planar sensitivity and the spatial resolution during experimental 223Ra imaging, and to determine optimal imaging parameters.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: A vial type source containing 223Ra solution (4.55 MBq / 5.6 ml) was placed in the air at 100 mm away from the collimator surface. Planar images were acquired with LEHR, LMEGP, ELEGP and MEGP collimators on two dual-head gamma cameras (Symbia intevo (Siemens) and Infinia 3 (GE)). We compared three energy window combinations: 1) single window at 82 keV, 2) double window at 82+154 keV, 3) triple window at 82+154+270 keV. The energy spectrum, the sensitivity and the spatial resolution, such as full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) and full-width at tenth-maximum (FWTM), of each collimator were assessed.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Five energy spectra (at around 82, 154, 270, 351 and 405 keV) were essentially observed among four collimators. The sensitivity was high for LEHR collimator, then ELEGP and LMEGP collimator was 3-4 fold, which is greater than MEGP collimator. The 82 keV energy window of four collimators has best spatial resolution. Moreover, the spatial resolution of the 82 keV energy window with LMEGP and ELEGP collimator was almost equal to that of the triple window with MEGP collimator.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Optimal imaging parameters were single energy window using LMEGP or ELEGP, and then triple energy window using MEGP collimator.
